inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL cash-flow-statement 'Stock-based compensation' add-back (FY2025 $1,592M) plus KPI 'equity_award_taxes' (cash tax withheld on net-share settlement, FY2025 $561M); Airbnb's 10-K does not publish a single combined equity-award figure in the adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation, so the two lines are summed per the fallback rule. FY2023's equity_award_taxes ($1,224M) is an outlier tied to heavy post-IPO-lockup RSU vesting; FY2024 ($630M) and FY2025 ($561M) show the normalized run-rate.
inputs.share_count_basis: Most recent reported shares_outstanding (Q2 2026, 597M), used as fully-diluted proxy and held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in owner FCF (charging both would double-count); count has been declining steadily (680M FY2022 -> 597M Q2 2026) funded by an active buyback program ($3.4B remaining authorization as of Jun-2026), consistent with a flat forward count.
inputs.price_as_of: Yahoo Finance chart API regular close, 2026-09-24 20:00:01 UTC; 52-week range 110.81-193.453
inputs.wacc_rationale: 9.0% base WACC for a large-cap USD-denominated, net-cash tech marketplace with investment-grade credit rating (senior notes issued Q1-2026 at 4.40%-5.25%); reflects ~4.2% risk-free (10yr UST, 2026) + ~4.8% levered equity-risk premium appropriate for a still-double-digit-growth consumer platform with regulatory/cyclical exposure. Bull -1pp (8.0%) for lower-risk execution on established growth drivers; bear +2pp (11.0%) for regulatory/competitive/macro risk stacking, consistent with charging cyclical/execution risk once (in the scenario driver paths) rather than in WACC alone, though a modest scenario-WACC spread is retained here given the binary regulatory-ban risk profile (NYC precedent) that is not fully captured by growth/margin paths alone.
inputs.lease_treatment: not material — Airbnb's own office/lease footprint is small relative to the balance sheet; no separate lease adjustment applied.
inputs.nci_treatment: none — wholly owned, no minority interests.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, scenario-weighted (SKILL.md routing: consumer-internet/marketplace operating company). 10-year explicit horizon because FY2025 owner-FCF margin (~18.6%, or ~20% ex the FY2023 RSU-vesting anomaly) is still below the ~22% mature margin implied by management's 'at least 35.5%' and rising adjusted-EBITDA-margin guidance -- a 5yr horizon would capitalize an immature margin. DATA GAP: no Extracted/ filing text exists for this SEC XBRL-only ticker (research/ABNB/Extracted/ is empty), so interest income ($200M/yr estimated at ~3.5-4.5% yield on the cash-only net-cash position, which understates Airbnb's true liquidity since the DB's cash_and_equivalents line excludes marketable securities held elsewhere on the balance sheet) and capex for FY2023-2025 (estimated at 0.15-0.20% of revenue, extrapolating the FY2019-2022 declining trend of 2.6% -> 1.1% -> 0.42% -> 0.30% of revenue, since the CSV/DB has no capex figure for those years) are ESTIMATES, not filing-sourced figures. Both are small relative to the FCF base (interest income ~9% of owner FCF, capex <2% of revenue) so the estimation risk is second-order, but a future update should replace them with figures read from the actual 10-K once filing text is extracted.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: blend of revenue_3yr_cagr (13.4%) and equity_3yr_cagr (13.8%); used as the anchor for base-case Year-1 growth before decelerating toward a ~4.5% terminal rate
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (8.6%, 2022->2025) is materially below revenue (13.4%) and equity (13.8%) CAGRs -- SBC (inclusive of equity-award cash taxes) has been growing roughly in line with or faster than owner FCF, and FY2023 in particular saw a post-IPO-lockup RSU-vesting bulge ($1,224M of equity-award taxes vs $607M FY2022 and $630M FY2024) that depressed that year's owner-FCF margin to 13.1% from a 20-22% run-rate either side of it. The divergence is a genuine SBC-dilution signal, not solely a one-off: an increasing share of Airbnb's reported growth is still being paid for in stock (SBC-incl-taxes was 17.6% of revenue in FY2025), which is why the forward SBC% path in this model only glides down gradually (16.5% -> 10.0%) rather than assuming rapid convergence to a low-SBC steady state.

base.narrative: FY2026 growth lands at the top of management's raised 'at least mid-teens' guidance (15%), then decelerates smoothly toward a 4.5% terminal rate as the ~44%-share leader's growth normalizes toward travel-industry (~5% nominal) trend. Adjusted EBITDA margin expands from the guided 'at least 35.5%' floor to a 38% mature level as Services/Experiences scale and AI cuts product/support cost (management cites AI already handling ~half of customer-service tickets). SBC-incl-equity-taxes glides from 17.6% of revenue toward 10% as the post-IPO-lockup RSU bulge fully normalizes and grant sizes moderate with a maturing employee base. Cash tax rate ramps from the current NOL-shielded ~10-12% toward a 24% blended statutory rate over the decade as carryforwards deplete. Working-capital capture of 13% on revenue growth reflects the deferred-revenue (guest-payment-in-advance) tailwind, which the FY2025 print already shows moderating (11.2% vs 16.1% FY2023, 15.9% FY2024) as growth itself decelerates.

bull.narrative: First-time booker growth keeps accelerating (11% YoY in Q2 2026, a 4-year high), Services and Experiences scale into a meaningful new GBV pool beyond Stays, and the 2027 AI travel agent becomes a genuine demand-generation and conversion advantage rather than a defensive move -- letting Airbnb win the AI-interface layer instead of being disintermediated by it. EBITDA margin expands further (toward a Booking-Holdings-like ~41%) as AI compresses concept-to-launch time and support cost structurally, and regulatory bans stay pocketed (NYC-style) rather than spreading to Airbnb's largest markets.

bear.narrative: Regulatory bans (the NYC precedent) spread to more major-metro markets, structurally shrinking addressable host supply; Booking.com and hotel loyalty programs keep taking share as they push further into alternative accommodations, compressing take rate; Services/Experiences investment ($200M+/yr) fails to scale into a durable new revenue line and stays a margin drag rather than a diversification win; and travel spending softens in a discretionary-spending downturn, consistent with the September 2026 sector-wide selloff (ABNB -10%+ over two sessions on sentiment alone). AI travel agents from OpenAI/Google-class entrants intermediate a growing share of trip planning before Airbnb's own 2027 agent ships, eroding the direct demand-side relationship the network-effect moat depends on.

scenario_narratives.base: Growth decelerates smoothly from the top of raised FY2026 guidance (mid-teens) to a ~4.5% terminal rate as the category leader's growth normalizes; EBITDA margin expands from the guided 35.5% floor to 38% as Services/Experiences and AI-driven cost efficiency mature; SBC glides down from a still-heavy 17.6% of revenue as post-IPO-lockup vesting normalizes.
scenario_narratives.bull: First-time-booker acceleration, successful Services/Experiences scaling, and a 2027 AI agent that wins rather than loses the AI-interface layer combine to sustain higher growth and push margins toward Booking-Holdings-like maturity (~41% EBITDA).
scenario_narratives.bear: Regulatory bans spread beyond NYC, Booking.com/hotel-loyalty competition compresses take rate, Services/Experiences investment fails to pay back, and third-party AI agents disintermediate direct bookings ahead of Airbnb's own 2027 launch, all against a discretionary-travel-spending downturn.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default 15/50/35 retained. Bear held at the default (not raised) because the balance sheet carries essentially no refinancing or solvency risk (investment-grade rated, net cash position, $2.5B notes issued Q1-2026 at fixed rates out to 2036) -- the bear case here is a margin/growth-compression story, not a going-concern one. Bull is not raised above 35% despite genuine embedded optionality (Services/Experiences/AI agent) because each of those requires several largely independent things to go right (new-category product-market fit, AI-interface competitive positioning, and continued share gains against a well-capitalized Booking Holdings), consistent with the method's guidance to hold bull weight down when the upside case needs multiple things to work.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Airbnb is a high-margin, asset-light, net-cash two-sided marketplace with a durable network-effect moat (~44% share of the short-term-rental category) generating real, growing owner free cash flow after fully expensing a still-heavy SBC charge. The house-basis probability-weighted intrinsic value lands almost exactly at today's price after the September 2026 sector-wide pullback (ABNB -10%+ over two sessions on sentiment, not fundamentals) -- consistent with a quality business that re-rated from expensive to roughly fair, with asymmetric optionality (Services, Experiences, the 2027 AI agent) providing bull-case upside that is not required to hold the base-case valuation together.
key_risks_to_valuation: Regulatory bans/restrictions on short-term rentals spreading beyond precedent cities (NYC) to larger markets
AI disintermediation: third-party AI travel agents winning the interface layer before Airbnb's own 2027 launch
Services/Experiences investment failing to scale into a durable, profitable revenue line
Discretionary consumer/travel spending cyclicality amplifying any macro slowdown

Data-gap risk: interest income and FY2023-2025 capex are ESTIMATED (no Extracted filing text available for this XBRL-only ticker) rather than read directly off the 10-K; both are small relative to the FCF base but should be verified against filing text on the next update
